precepts.text: After the Exodus: ye are the children of the Lord your God. We are the sons of God.
precepts.point: After the Most High sent the flood, those same spirits came right back through the three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth. There is no new thing under the sun.

note.label: Popular Persuasions: Fighting Against Heaven Defending Earth

precepts.why:
The sons of God in Genesis 6 are Adam’s line, the lineage traced in Genesis 5. Did that name change later, after the flood and after Egypt? No. Deuteronomy 14:1, spoken after the Exodus, says to Israel: “Ye are the children of the Lord your God.”

We are the children of the Lord our God because we are the sons of God. The same people carried the same title from Adam through Noah, through the fathers, out of Egypt, and into the law.

This matters for reading Genesis 6 rightly. The sons of God who went in to the daughters of men were not angels coming down from the sky; they were men of that same chosen line, God’s own children, who mixed with the other nations when it was forbidden. That sin brought the flood, and later the affliction of our people. The scriptures do not change the name: from Genesis, to Deuteronomy, to the prophets, to the New Testament, it is our people who are called the children and the sons of God.

precepts.text: That which dieth of itself is given to the stranger in thy gates or sold to an alien; thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God.
precepts.point: Always get the context of the law, because sometimes the stranger is your brother and sometimes it is literally the other nations. Deuteronomy 14:21 doubles this law: that which dieth of itself thou shalt give unto the stranger that is in thy gates, or sell it unto an alien, for thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God. Cast the torn flesh to the other nations; ye shall not eat it, because ye are holy people.

note.label: Exodus 22: The Civil Laws of Restitution

precepts.why:
“And ye shall be holy men unto me: neither shall ye eat any flesh that is torn of beasts in the field; ye shall cast it to the dogs.” This is twofold, and the dogs are the strangers of other nations, the aliens and foreigners. Deuteronomy 14:21 doubles the law and names them: “Ye shall not eat of any thing that dieth of itself: thou shalt give it unto the stranger that is in thy gates, that he may eat it; or thou mayest sell it unto an alien: for thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God.”

Always get the context of the law, because sometimes the stranger is your brother and sometimes it is literally the other nations. Here it is the other nations: cast the torn flesh to them, give it to the stranger in thy gates or sell it to an alien. Ye shall not eat it, because ye are holy people unto the Lord thy God.

precepts.text: The thing that dieth of itself may be given to the stranger or sold to an alien, for thou art an holy people; the law marks the difference between Israel and the nations.
precepts.point: That which dieth of itself, or is torn with beasts, he shall not eat to defile himself therewith. That same law elsewhere says to give such a thing unto the stranger or sell it to an alien, for thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God: these laws were given to Israel alone, and the other nations may eat those things because they are not the holy people. There is no equality in that.

note.label: Leviticus 22: The Holy Things and Offerings Without Blemish

precepts.why:
“That which dieth of itself, or is torn with beasts, he shall not eat to defile himself therewith.” The same law elsewhere shows what was to be done with such a thing: “Ye shall not eat of any thing that dieth of itself: thou shalt give it unto the stranger that is in thy gates, that he may eat it; or thou mayest sell it unto an alien: for thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God.”

These laws were given to Israel alone. The other nations may eat those things because they are not the holy people; Israel may not, because “thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God.” The law marks the difference between Israel and the nations. There is no equality in that.

precepts.text: The Levite has no part nor inheritance with thee; the Levite, the stranger, the fatherless, and the widow within thy gates shall come and eat and be satisfied.
precepts.point: The money went to Aaron and the priests because they had to take care of the widows, the fatherless, and the strangers; the strangers are our people that come from different parts of the land down to Jerusalem needing help. That is how the Most High put money into the sanctuary to take care of those that could not take care of themselves.

note.label: Numbers 3: The Levites Taken Instead of the Firstborn

precepts.why:
The firstborn of Israel outnumbered the Levites by 273, and those odd ones were redeemed at “five shekels apiece by the poll, after the shekel of the sanctuary”, the shekel being twenty gerahs. Moses took that redemption money, 1,365 shekels, and gave it “unto Aaron and to his sons.”

Why did the money go to Aaron and the priests? “And the Levite that is within thy gates; thou shalt not forsake him; for he hath no part nor inheritance with thee.” The Levite had no inheritance of his own, and he had to take care of the widows, the fatherless and the strangers. At the end of three years the tithe of the increase was laid up within the gates, “And the Levite, (because he hath no part nor inheritance with thee,) and the stranger, and the fatherless, and the widow, which are within thy gates, shall come, and shall eat and be satisfied.”

The strangers are our people that come from different parts of the land down to Jerusalem needing help. That is how the Most High put money into the sanctuary to take care of those that could not take care of themselves, “that the Lord thy God may bless thee in all the work of thine hand which thou doest.”

precepts.text: Thou art an holy people, chosen to be a peculiar people unto himself, above all the nations upon the earth; Deuteronomy 7 likewise calls Israel special and above all nations.
precepts.point: Which shall hear all these statutes and say, surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people: they may not say it out loud today, but when they see Israel united in Christ and in order, that is what rises in their minds.

note.label: Deuteronomy 4: Neither Add nor Diminish

precepts.why:
“For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God, and the Lord hath chosen thee to be a peculiar people unto himself, above all the nations that are upon the earth.” Deuteronomy 7 likewise calls Israel special and above all nations.

Peculiar means characteristic of only one person, group or thing, and different from the usual or normal. The Most High made this people different and set them above the other nations, and keeping the laws is what makes them so. That is why “Keep therefore and do them; for this is your wisdom and your understanding in the sight of the nations”. Israel deals with the Almighty, and having the omnipotent God on your side is the wisdom the nations do not have, and it is what they are mad at.

precepts.text: Thou shalt not eat any abominable thing; the lusting of the soul sits inside the dietary law.
precepts.point: The unclean and the clean that may eat thereof are unclean and clean persons, not unclean meats; Israel had servants then and will have servants again.

note.label: Deuteronomy 12: The Place Where the Lord Puts His Name

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not eat any abominable thing.” “whatsoever thy soul lusteth after” is not license to eat anything. The lusting of the soul sits inside the dietary law: it stays within the guidelines of the clean foods, “as of the roebuck, and as of the hart”, the beasts listed in chapter 14. Whatever the soul lusts after has to be one of those, because the law says thou shalt not eat any abominable thing.

So the freedom to kill and eat flesh in all thy gates, “according to the blessing of the Lord thy God which he hath given thee”, is freedom within the clean foods, never outside them.

precepts.text: Fourscore men came with their beards shaven, their clothes rent, and having cut themselves; an example of the cutting practice the law forbids.
precepts.point: Cutting the flesh was a form of self-torture in mourning; the Most High requires none of that of us, only to be righteous and keep his commandments.

note.label: Deuteronomy 14: A Peculiar People and the Clean Foods

precepts.why:
“Ye are the children of the Lord your God: ye shall not cut yourselves, nor make any baldness between your eyes for the dead.” Jeremiah shows the very practice the law forbids: “there came certain from Shechem, from Shiloh, and from Samaria, even fourscore men, having their beards shaven, and their clothes rent, and having cut themselves, with offerings and incense in their hand, to bring them to the house of the Lord.”

Fourscore men, beards shaven, clothes rent, and cut themselves, coming to the house of the Lord that way. Cutting the flesh was a form of self-torture in mourning, and these customs came from the other nations. It is like the young folks today cutting designs into their eyebrows; we are not supposed to be doing that.

The Most High requires none of that of us, only to be righteous and keep his commandments.

precepts.text: Ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; the same title as Deuteronomy 14:2.
precepts.point: Israel became strangers in the day they were displaced out of their homeland, as Obadiah says of the day of Jacob's captivity. The peculiar people given the peculiar laws of God is Israel, and that is what is taught to our people today, raising them back up into the understanding of who they are and that we must repent in order to get the kingdom.

note.label: Deuteronomy 14: A Peculiar People and the Clean Foods

precepts.why:
“For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God, and the Lord hath chosen thee to be a peculiar people unto himself, above all the nations that are upon the earth.” Peter writes to that same peculiar people: “But ye are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation, a peculiar people; that ye should shew forth the praises of him who hath called you out of darkness into his marvellous light”.

It is the same title Moses gave Israel: an holy nation, a peculiar people. The peculiar people given the peculiar laws of God is Israel, and Peter's letter is addressed to them, the strangers scattered through Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia.

That is what is taught to our people today: raising them back up into the understanding of who they are, and that we must repent in order to get the kingdom.

precepts.text: Peter writes to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia.
precepts.point: Israel became strangers in the day they were displaced out of their homeland, as Obadiah says of the day of Jacob's captivity. The peculiar people given the peculiar laws of God is Israel, and that is what is taught to our people today, raising them back up into the understanding of who they are and that we must repent in order to get the kingdom.

note.label: Deuteronomy 14: A Peculiar People and the Clean Foods

precepts.why:
Who is the peculiar people Peter writes to? His letter opens: “Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia”. The chosen generation and peculiar people of his letter are these strangers, scattered through those regions.

Who were those strangers? Acts 2 answers it: Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven, dwelling in the very regions Peter lists, Cappadocia, Pontus, and Asia. That is one way to prove who the strangers of the New Testament are.

They are Israel, the peculiar people of Deuteronomy 14:2, become strangers in the day they were displaced out of their homeland.

precepts.text: There were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.
precepts.point: Israel became strangers in the day they were displaced out of their homeland, as Obadiah says of the day of Jacob's captivity. The peculiar people given the peculiar laws of God is Israel, and that is what is taught to our people today, raising them back up into the understanding of who they are and that we must repent in order to get the kingdom.

note.label: Deuteronomy 14: A Peculiar People and the Clean Foods

precepts.why:
“And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.” Here are Peter's strangers: Jews, devout men, scattered out of every nation under heaven.

Read on to verse 9 and the regions they came from are named, Cappadocia, Pontus, and Asia, the same places Peter's letter was sent to. So the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia are Jews, and the peculiar people Peter calls them is the peculiar people the Lord chose above all the nations that are upon the earth.

That is one way to prove who the strangers of the New Testament are.

precepts.text: The dwellers in Mesopotamia, Judaea, Cappadocia, Pontus, and Asia; the same regions where Peter's strangers were scattered.
precepts.point: Israel became strangers in the day they were displaced out of their homeland, as Obadiah says of the day of Jacob's captivity. The peculiar people given the peculiar laws of God is Israel, and that is what is taught to our people today, raising them back up into the understanding of who they are and that we must repent in order to get the kingdom.

note.label: Deuteronomy 14: A Peculiar People and the Clean Foods

precepts.why:
“Parthians, and Medes, and Elamites, and the dwellers in Mesopotamia, and in Judea, and Cappadocia, in Pontus, and Asia”. The Jews dwelling at Jerusalem out of every nation came from Cappadocia, Pontus, and Asia, the very regions Peter names when he writes “to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia”.

Line the two up and it is one way to prove who the strangers of the New Testament are: Jews, Israel, scattered among the nations. So when Peter calls his readers a chosen generation and a peculiar people, he is speaking to the same people Moses spoke to, chosen to be a peculiar people above all the nations that are upon the earth.

precepts.text: The day that he became a stranger: Israel became strangers when they were displaced out of their homeland.
precepts.point: Israel became strangers in the day they were displaced out of their homeland, as Obadiah says of the day of Jacob's captivity. The peculiar people given the peculiar laws of God is Israel, and that is what is taught to our people today, raising them back up into the understanding of who they are and that we must repent in order to get the kingdom.

note.label: Deuteronomy 14: A Peculiar People and the Clean Foods

precepts.why:
How did the peculiar people become strangers? Obadiah speaks of “the day of thy brother in the day that he became a stranger”, “the children of Judah in the day of their destruction”, “the day of distress”. Israel became strangers in the day they were displaced out of their homeland, the day of Jacob's captivity.

That is why Peter writes to strangers scattered: the peculiar people chosen above all the nations were scattered out of their land and made strangers in it.

The peculiar people given the peculiar laws of God is Israel, and that is what is taught to our people today, raising them back up into the understanding of who they are and that we must repent in order to get the kingdom.

precepts.text: Whatsoever thy soul lusteth after, as of the roebuck and as of the hart: the lusting of the soul is bounded by the clean beasts of this chapter.
precepts.point: The chapter then lists the clean beasts, the beasts that part the hoof and chew the cud, the fish with fins and scales, and the clean fowls; the rest of chapter 14 is clear cut on the laws of the clean and the unclean foods.

note.label: Deuteronomy 14: A Peculiar People and the Clean Foods

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not eat any abominable thing” rules the whole chapter. Chapter 12 said “thou mayest kill and eat flesh in all thy gates, whatsoever thy soul lusteth after, according to the blessing of the Lord thy God which he hath given thee: the unclean and the clean may eat thereof, as of the roebuck, and as of the hart.”

That whatsoever thy soul lusteth after sits inside the guidelines of clean foods: as of the roebuck, as of the hart, clean beasts. The lusting of the soul is bounded by the clean beasts of this chapter; you cannot eat anything you want.

Some of our people, still unlearned, think that as long as they pray over it they can eat it. That is not true; it is a misunderstanding carried out of the New Testament. The law says thou shalt not eat any abominable thing, and the chapter then lists the clean beasts, the beasts that part the hoof and chew the cud, the fish with fins and scales, and the clean fowls. The rest of chapter 14 is clear cut on the laws of the clean and the unclean foods.

precepts.text: Hearken diligently and he gives the rain in due season, that thou mayest gather thy corn, thy wine, and thine oil; the increase that is tithed is the increase he gives.
precepts.point: Today Israel is disconnected from that fear because the oppressor nourishes us; the food comes from the grocery store. That understanding must be brought back to our people, and that is why the laws are read four chapters a day, from Genesis all the way to Revelation, to gain the understanding that we are the Israelites.

note.label: Deuteronomy 14: A Peculiar People and the Clean Foods

precepts.why:
The tithe is of “thy corn, of thy wine, and of thine oil”, the increase of thy seed year by year. Chapter 11 shows where that increase comes from: “if ye shall hearken diligently unto my commandments which I command you this day, to love the Lord your God, and to serve him with all your heart and with all your soul, That I will give you the rain of your land in his due season, the first rain and the latter rain, that thou mayest gather in thy corn, and thy wine, and thine oil.”

The corn, wine, and oil tithed here are the same corn, wine, and oil promised in chapter 11 for hearkening to the commandments; this all goes together. The increase that is tithed is the increase he gives.

If Israel did not keep the commandments, he would shut up the heaven, there would be no rain, the land would be chapt, and famine would teach the fear of the Lord. That is the tithe eaten before him “that thou mayest learn to fear the Lord thy God always.”

Today Israel is disconnected from that fear because the oppressor nourishes us; the food comes from the grocery store. That understanding must be brought back to our people, and that is why the laws are read four chapters a day, from Genesis all the way to Revelation, to gain the understanding that we are the Israelites.

precepts.text: Thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God, chosen to be a peculiar people above all the nations upon the earth.
precepts.point: Ezekiel says it plainly: the children of Israel eat their defiled bread among the Gentiles. Others may eat that food, but it is foul for us because we are supposed to eat the best food on the planet, for we are an holy people as Deuteronomy 14 says.

note.label: Deuteronomy 28: The Blessings and the Curses That Identify Israel

precepts.why:
“For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God, and the Lord hath chosen thee to be a peculiar people unto himself, above all the nations that are upon the earth.” That is why the cursed food hits us the way it does. Others may eat the fast food and the unclean meat from the corner store, but it is foul for us: an holy people, chosen above all the nations upon the earth, is supposed to eat the best food on the planet.

Instead the fruit of the land, the kine and the sheep are cursed to us, and we eat our defiled bread among the Gentiles, as Ezekiel says. And the fruit of our body, our children, is cursed with it.

precepts.text: The tithe turned to money could be bestowed for whatsoever the soul lusteth after, meaning oxen, sheep, wine, and food, not sex.
precepts.point: Nothing is said of her being pregnant. The Ethiopian tradition claims Solomon fathered a son with her and founded a dynasty, but the scripture gives no such thing; she turned and went to her own country with her servants.

note.label: 1 Kings 10: The Queen of Sheba and the Riches of Solomon

precepts.why:
When the way was too long to carry the tithe, Israel could turn it into money, “And thou shalt bestow that money for whatsoever thy soul lusteth after, for oxen, or for sheep, or for wine, or for strong drink, or for whatsoever thy soul desireth: and thou shalt eat there before the Lord thy God, and thou shalt rejoice”. Whatsoever the soul lusteth after means oxen, sheep, wine and food, not sex. The word desire in scripture does not always mean what people think.

So when “king Solomon gave unto the queen of Sheba all her desire, whatsoever she asked”, people assume it was sexual. But her desire was to know his wisdom and see his order.

Nothing is said of her being pregnant. The Ethiopian tradition claims Solomon fathered a son with her and founded a dynasty, but the scripture gives no such thing: “So she turned and went to her own country, she and her servants.”

precepts.text: Thou shalt not forsake the Levite within thy gates, for he has no part nor inheritance with thee.
precepts.point: The great sin the account underlines is Jeroboam casting off the Levites, a law the Most High was very specific about.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 13: Abijah Stands on the Covenant

precepts.why:
“And the Levite that is within thy gates; thou shalt not forsake him; for he hath no part nor inheritance with thee.”

The great sin the account underlines is Jeroboam casting off the Levites, and this is a law the Most High was very specific about. Thou shalt not forsake the Levite. Jeroboam did, and Abijah, who stood on the covenant and kept the priests of the Lord, “waxed mighty.”

precepts.text: Truly tithe all the increase year by year, and do not forsake the Levite within your gates, for he has no part nor inheritance with you.
precepts.point: They lay the tithe in heaps from the third to the seventh month, and when Hezekiah and the princes see the heaps they bless the Lord and his people Israel.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 31: The Tithe Restored

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt truly tithe all the increase of thy seed, that the field bringeth forth year by year.” The tithe of “thy corn, of thy wine, and of thine oil, and the firstlings of thy herds and of thy flocks” was brought “that thou mayest learn to fear the Lord thy God always.” And the charge ends: “the Levite that is within thy gates; thou shalt not forsake him; for he hath no part nor inheritance with thee.”

Hezekiah restored exactly that. He appointed the priests and Levites “after their courses, every man according to his service”, set “the king’s portion of his substance” for the morning and evening, sabbath, new moon and feast offerings, “as it is written in the law of the Lord”, and “commanded the people that dwelt in Jerusalem to give the portion of the priests and the Levites, that they might be encouraged in the law of the Lord.” The Levite was not forsaken.

“And as soon as the commandment came abroad, the children of Israel brought in abundance the firstfruits of corn, wine, and oil, and honey, and of all the increase of the field; and the tithe of all things brought they in abundantly.” They laid it by heaps from the third month to the seventh, “And when Hezekiah and the princes came and saw the heaps, they blessed the Lord, and his people Israel.”

precepts.text: The Most High chose Israel to be a peculiar people unto himself, above all the nations that are upon the earth.
precepts.point: Therefore the first letters sent by Haman are not to be executed, for Haman himself is hanged at the gates of Susa with all his family, the Most High rendering vengeance according to his deserts. The copy of this second letter is to be published everywhere so the Jews may live after their own laws and, on the thirteenth day of Adar, be avenged on those who set upon them.

note.label: Esther 16: The Second Letter and the Reversal

precepts.why:
The king's second letter finds the Jews “are no evildoers, but live by most just laws: And that they be children of the most high and most mighty, living God, who hath ordered the kingdom both unto us and to our progenitors in the most excellent manner.” A heathen king writes to every province that Israel are the children of the living God. That is the plain testimony of scripture concerning who Israel is.

The Most High said it first: “thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God, and the Lord hath chosen thee to be a peculiar people unto himself, above all the nations that are upon the earth.” Israel is his chosen, peculiar people, above all the nations. The first letter called them a malicious people whose laws were contrary to all nations; the second says the opposite, that their laws are most just and their God is the most high and most mighty. The king's letter caught up with what the Lord had already declared.

precepts.text: Coupled with Malachi, the tithe was tied to the Levitical priesthood; our duty now is alms.
precepts.point: He smote all the firstborn, the chief of all their strength. The firstborn is the chief of one's strength, as Reuben was Jacob's strength before he lost it.

note.label: Psalm 105: Remember His Marvelous Works from Abraham to the Exodus

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt truly tithe all the increase of thy seed, that the field bringeth forth year by year.” The tithe was of the increase of the seed, what the field brought forth, which is why Malachi calls it meat for the storehouse.

Coupled with Malachi, the tithe was tied to the Levitical priesthood. Our duty now is alms.

moments.label: Integrated but Divided: What Did We Lose?

points: I am reading this for you dumb Christians who are thinking that there is no segregation in the Bible.
For thou art an holy people — we are a separate people — unto the Lord thy God, and the Lord hath chosen thee to be a peculiar people unto himself, above all the nations that are upon the earth.

How many times does God have to say the same thing? We above. We above. We above. But the black man, the Hispanic man, the Native American man, they cannot see it. No, we equal. No, we are not equal. There is no equality.

note.label: Integrated but Divided: What Did We Lose?

points: What riches in the temple did not pertain to the sacrifices? The reading explained the collections: sustenance for the Levites, who had no territorial inheritance; support for the Aaronic priests, the tithe of the tithe; and every third year a community chest to feed local Levites, widows, orphans, and resident foreigners.

At the end of three years thou shalt bring forth all the tithe of thine increase, and the Levite, the stranger, and the fatherless, and the widow within thy gates shall come, and shall eat and be satisfied. The scripture tells you the monies collected were for the Levites, the strangers, the fatherless, and the widows.

note.label: From Brother To Betrayer

points: Ye are the children of the Lord your God: ye shall not cut yourselves, nor make any baldness between your eyes for the dead. These customs came from the other nations, like the young folks today cutting designs into their eyebrows; we are not supposed to be doing that.
Cutting the flesh was a form of self-torture in mourning; the Most High requires none of that of us, only to be righteous and keep his commandments.

note.label: Deuteronomy 14: A Peculiar People and the Clean Foods

points: Thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God, chosen to be a peculiar people unto himself above all the nations upon the earth.

Peter writes to that same peculiar people, a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, an holy nation: his letter is addressed to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia.

Who were those strangers? Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven, dwelling in the very regions Peter lists, Cappadocia, Pontus, and Asia; that is one way to prove who the strangers of the New Testament are.

Israel became strangers in the day they were displaced out of their homeland, as Obadiah says of the day of Jacob's captivity. The peculiar people given the peculiar laws of God is Israel, and that is what is taught to our people today, raising them back up into the understanding of who they are and that we must repent in order to get the kingdom.

note.label: Deuteronomy 14: A Peculiar People and the Clean Foods

points: Thou shalt not eat any abominable thing: this rules the whole chapter. The whatsoever thy soul lusteth after of chapter 12 sits inside these guidelines of clean foods; you cannot eat anything you want.

Some of our people, still unlearned, think that as long as they pray over it they can eat it; that is not true, it is a misunderstanding carried out of the New Testament. The law says thou shalt not eat any abominable thing.

The chapter then lists the clean beasts, the beasts that part the hoof and chew the cud, the fish with fins and scales, and the clean fowls; the rest of chapter 14 is clear cut on the laws of the clean and the unclean foods.

note.label: Deuteronomy 14: A Peculiar People and the Clean Foods

points: Thou shalt truly tithe all the increase of thy seed that the field bringeth forth year by year, and eat before the Lord the tithe of thy corn, of thy wine, and of thine oil, that thou mayest learn to fear the Lord thy God always.

The corn, wine, and oil are the same increase promised in chapter 11 for hearkening to the commandments; this all goes together. If Israel did not keep the commandments, he would shut up the heaven, there would be no rain, the land would be chapt, and famine would teach the fear of the Lord.
